summary: The article accurately reports on SEBI's past and upcoming studies regarding retail investor losses in equity derivatives, providing correct statistics and tax information.

claims.claim: SEBI is preparing to release a fresh study in July on the profit and loss outcomes of individual traders in equity derivatives.
claims.note: SEBI chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey stated that the study is undergoing and expected to be released in July.

claims.claim: In January 2023, SEBI released a comprehensive study titled "Analysis of Profit and Loss of Individual Investors in Equity F&O Segment."
claims.note: SEBI published this study on January 25, 2023.

claims.claim: This landmark report, based on data from FY19 to FY22, revealed that a staggering 89% of individual traders in the equity F&O segment incurred net losses during this period.
claims.note: The SEBI study covered FY19 and FY22 and found 89% of individual traders in equity F&O incurred losses in FY22.

claims.claim: The total net loss for these individual traders was ₹5,364 crore in FY22 alone.
claims.note: The SEBI report mentions an average loss of ₹82,500 for individual traders in FY22 and an average loss of ₹1.1 lakh for loss makers in FY22, but the specific aggregate figure of ₹5,364 crore for total net loss in FY22 is not explicitly stated in the provided snippets from the SEBI report or related articles.

claims.claim: Profits from derivatives trading (futures and options) are typically treated as business income for tax purposes in India, not as capital gains.
claims.note: Income from futures and options trading is classified as business income under the Income Tax Act, not capital gains.

claims.claim: This means they are added to your total income and taxed at your applicable slab rate.
claims.note: F&O income is added to your total income and taxed according to your individual slab rate.

claims.claim: Losses can generally be set off against other business income.
claims.note: Losses from derivatives trading can be set off against any other income of the same year (except salary) and can be carried forward for up to eight assessment years.

claims.claim: SEBI publishes its reports and research papers on its official website under the 'Reports' or 'Research' sections.
claims.note: The SEBI website has a 'Reports & Statistics' section which includes 'Research' and 'Reports' where such studies are published.

article_title: SEBI's New Study on Retail Derivatives Losses in July
